Simulated trading · paper only

Strategies by trade type, and what the recording says about them

Each strategy is a trade type with an explicit entry rule, exit rule and fee model. They are replayed against the recorded price paths in data/candles.json. A fill is only booked where an executable quote existed in that recording; when there is no counterparty the trade is skipped and the reason is counted. This page never claims a live demo-account balance, because no API key exists here.

Why most strategies traded nothing

This is the honest part of the exercise. The recording is one instrument with a permanently one-sided book (bids 0.14, no NO bids, offers pinned at 1.00). Strategies that require a two-sided quote or a cheap ask therefore have no executable entry, and the engine refuses to invent one. The skip counters below are the proof.

Fee model, in full

Kalshi's published schedule charges the taker ceil_centicent(M × 0.07 × C × P × (1 − P)) and the maker 0.0175 instead of 0.07 when a resting order later fills. The replay above uses the taker rate, because every entry is modelled as crossing the spread. This matters: a $0.10 gross move on a 100-contract 50-cent position is $10.00, of which $1.75 is fee on the way in and about $1.75 on the way out. Read the official fee schedule ↗

How to run this yourself against real demo-account data

  1. Create a demo API key in the Kalshi demo UI and keep it outside the repository.
  2. Read the account with GET /portfolio/balance (its own rate-limit bucket, 1 req/s on Basic).
  3. Place orders with V2 POST /portfolio/events/orders — the legacy /portfolio/orders write endpoints now return 410 Gone.
  4. Send side as bid (≡ yes) or ask (≡ no), with price as a fixed-point dollar string and count as a *_fp string.

Sources: Create Order (V2) · order direction · Get Balance
